div.head: VII Atr 2.4
div.ab: Si quis ieiunium suum infringat, seruus corio suo componat, liber pauper reddat XXX denarios et tainus regis CXX sol.; et diuidatur hec pecunia pauperibus.
Si quis ieiunium suum infringat, servus corio suo componat, liber pauper reddat XXX denarios et tainus regis CXX sol.; et dividatur haec pecunia pauperibus.
Si quis ieiunium suum infringat, servus corio suo componat, liber pauper reddat XXX denarios et tainus regis CXX sol.; et dividatur hec pecunia pauperibus.
Wenn jemand sein Fasten bricht, büsse der Sklav mit seiner Haut, zahle ein armer Freier 30 Pfennig und ein Königsthegn 120 Schill.; und dies Geld werde den Armen vertheilt.
If anyone breaks his fast, let a slave pay with his hide, a poor freeman pay 30 pence and a king's thegn 120 shillings; and let this money be distributed to the poor.

In the case of the fast being broken—if it is a slave [who does so], he shall undergo the lash, if it is a poor freeman, he shall pay 30 pence, and a thegn of the king's [shall pay] 120 shillings. And this money shall be divided among the poor.
If anyone breaks the fast: a slave is to be whipped, a poor freeman is to pay thirty pence and a king’s thane one hundred twenty shillings; and this money is to be distributed to the poor.
div.note: ebd. 3 | Vgl. E Gu. 8 | VIIa Poen. 4
Liebermann compares EGu and VIIa Atr 3.; AU: corrected against Rabin p. 182 / 183, October 2026 (was “xxx; cxx”, now “XXX; CXX”)
one hundred twenty shillings: This amount is likely an error, as analogous passages elsewhere set the penalty for breaking the fast at only thirty shillings.

þræl mid his hide VIIa; þoljan þære hyde Hom. 172; cf. Gl Fasten 3b. 5a

bunda VIIa, bonda Hom. 172; s. über das Wort o. S. 171 Z. 1. Es entspricht hier der Klasse ceorl und bedeutet (wie dieses) erst viel später den Unfreien. Die 30 Pf. sind ein Strafgeldfixum (s. d. Gl 9) für ähnliche Vergehen, gleich dem Wert eines Ochsen, der Versäumnisbusse des Peterspfennigs; s. d. Gl 17a ff.

bunda VIIa, bonda Hom. 172; on the word see above p. 171 l. 1. Here it corresponds to the class ceorl and (like that word) comes to mean the unfree man only much later. The 30 pence are a fixed fine (see that word in Gl 9) for similar offences, equal to the value of an ox, the penalty for neglecting Peter’s Pence; see that word in Gl 17a ff.

þegn XXX scil. VIIa 3; Homil. 172 (s. ebd. 12). Vielleicht ist dies kein Widerspruch hiergegen, sondern dieses Reichsgesetz berücksichtigte nur die höchsten (des Königs) Thegnas, dagegen das für eine Stiftskirche bearbeitete Bussedikt nur die mittelbaren.—Die 120 Schill. sind ‘Ungehorsam’ (s. d. Gl 6. 7), der bei ähnlichem Anlass verwirkt wird.—Strafgeld an die Armen auch As Alm 2

þegn XXX scil. VIIa 3; Homil. 172 (see ibid. 12). Perhaps this does not contradict the present passage; rather, this law of the realm took account only of the highest thegns (the king’s), whereas the penitential edict, drawn up for a collegiate church, took account only of the mediate ones.—The 120 shill. are ‘disobedience’ (see that word in Gl 6. 7), which is forfeited on similar occasions.—A fine paid to the poor also in As Alm 2
Cf. VII Atr. A.S. 3; E. and G. 8.
